event_info.event_description: Analyze for disclosures on global pandemic risks. Look for corporate language discussing widespread impacts like supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, remote work transitions, and fundamental shifts in consumer demand.

holistic_analysis: CDW’s 2022 Form 10-K frames COVID-19 as both an already-realized shock and an enduring, forward-looking threat across every major operational dimension—supply chain continuity, labour availability, customer demand, logistics, cost inflation and liquidity.  The company states that it has “experienced” concrete disruptions (e.g., supply shortages, facility closures, delivery bottlenecks) and cost increases, while simultaneously warning that resurgences, new variants and government mandates could intensify these pressures.  Language is specific (naming supply chain partners, facilities and labour functions), repeatedly uses “materially” and “adversely,” and links the pandemic to fundamental metrics such as cash flows, results of operations and liquidity.  Because the filing date (28 Feb 2022) falls less than three years after the WHO declaration (11 Mar 2020), the Time Decay Principle permits high severity scores; no mitigating statements of equal weight (e.g., comprehensive risk controls or quantified offsets) are provided.  Overall, the risk evidence is recent, direct and multi-faceted, warranting upper-tier scores in the 6-9 range for individual snippets.

evidence_list.snippet: The outbreak of the novel coronavirus (“COVID-19”) pandemic has adversely impacted and could continue to adversely impact our business and results of operations and could also adversely impact our cash flows, financial condition and liquidity.

components.reason: Explicitly cites COVID-19 as the cause of impact (direct event linkage).
States impacts have already occurred (“has adversely impacted”).
Projects continued future impact.
Covers multiple critical financial dimensions (cash flows, liquidity).

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Direct mention, realised harm and forward-looking risk across key financial metrics justify a high score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: We have experienced and could continue to experience disruptions, including as a result of resurgences of COVID-19, that prevent us from meeting the demands of our customers, such as product constraints from our vendor partners and wholesale distributors and other disruptions to our supply chain, disruptions in or restrictions on the ability of our coworkers to work effectively, temporary closures of our distribution facilities, modifications in the operation of facilities that remain open and disruptions of commercial delivery services.

components.reason: Direct reference to COVID-19 resurgences.
Admits past disruptions already felt.
Enumerates detailed supply-chain and labour breakdowns.
Highlights inability to meet customer demand—core operational threat.
Covers multiple facility and logistics shutdown scenarios, broadening severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Past and potential future operational breakdowns across supply chain, labour and logistics earn near-maximum severity (9).

evidence_list.snippet: The impact of COVID-19 and measures implemented to slow the spread have caused and could continue to cause delay in, or limit the ability of, our customers to place orders for our products and services and make timely payments to us and could materially increase our labor, logistics and other costs.

components.reason: Explicit COVID-19 linkage.
Confirms historical impact on customer ordering and payments.
Identifies dual pressure: revenue delays and cost escalation.
Uses ‘materially increase’ signalling significant magnitude.
Projects continued future impact.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Combination of realised revenue disruption and material cost inflation yields a strong score of 8.

evidence_list.snippet: As long as the pandemic continues, our coworkers will continue to be exposed to health risks, and we could be negatively impacted in the future if a significant number of our coworkers, or coworkers who perform critical functions, become unable to work as a result of exposure to COVID-19.

components.reason: Direct mention of COVID-19 exposure.
Highlights threat to critical workforce availability (business continuity).
Frames risk as ongoing for the duration of the pandemic.
Potential for significant operational impact if many workers incapacitated.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Focused labour-continuity risk tied to ongoing pandemic earns a solid 7.

evidence_list.snippet: During the COVID-19 pandemic and even after it has subsided, we may experience adverse impacts to our business as a result of the pandemic’s global economic impact, including any recession, economic downturn or volatility, government spending cuts, tightening of credit markets or increased unemployment that has occurred or may occur in the future, which could cause our customers and potential customers to postpone or reduce spending on technology products or services or put downward pressure on prices.

components.reason: Explicit COVID-19 reference.
Links to broad macroeconomic fallout (recession, credit tightening).
Directly ties macro effects to reduced customer spending and pricing pressure.
Notes persistence of risk even post-pandemic.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Macro-economic demand risk that extends into the future justifies a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: The proposed federal vaccinate mandate, along with any other vaccine requirements applicable to our coworkers, and the uncertainty and unpredictability of the COVID-19 environment, could make it more difficult to attract or retain key personnel.

components.reason: Direct COVID-19 context tied to regulatory mandates.
Specifies talent attraction & retention risk—critical human-capital factor.
Highlights uncertainty and unpredictability, increasing difficulty in planning.
Potential, not yet realised, lowers severity slightly.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Regulatory-driven labour risk is clear but still contingent, warranting a moderate-high score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: A sustained labor shortage or increased turnover rates within our coworker base, whether caused by COVID-19 or as a result of general macroeconomic factors occurring throughout the US economy, could lead to increased costs, such as increased overtime to meet demand and increased wage rates to attract and retain coworkers, and could adversely affect our business, results of operations or cash flows.

components.reason: Attributes possible labour shortage directly to COVID-19 among other factors.
Details concrete cost impacts (overtime, wage inflation).
Connects to adverse effects on operations and cash flows.
Risk is prospective (‘could’), slightly tempering severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Prospective but financially explicit labour-cost pressure merits a score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: Additionally, strikes, inclement weather, natural disasters or other service interruptions by such shippers or periods of increased demand on delivery services, such as those we have experienced during the COVID-19 pandemic, could materially adversely affect our ability to deliver or receive products on a timely basis.

components.reason: Refers to actual pandemic-era delivery bottlenecks (‘we have experienced’).
Highlights logistics and fulfilment risk critical to operations.
Uses strong materiality language (‘materially adversely’).
Specifies both past experience and future possibility.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Confirmed past logistics disruption with material language leads to a score of 7.

evidence_list.snippet: If our customers’ businesses are adversely affected by the impact of COVID-19, they may delay or reduce purchases from us, which could adversely affect our results of operations.

components.reason: Directly links customer demand risk to COVID-19.
Describes potential revenue reduction through delayed/ reduced purchases.
Notes adverse effect on results of operations.
Risk is conditional (‘if’), moderating severity.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Conditional but clear demand-side revenue risk generates a score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: The global spread of the novel coronavirus (“COVID-19”) pandemic continues to create macroeconomic uncertainty, volatility and disruption, including supply constraints.

components.reason: Explicit COVID-19 reference.
Describes ongoing (‘continues’) macro-level uncertainty and disruption.
Identifies specific operational issue—supply constraints.
Broadly affects strategic planning and forecasting.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Ongoing macro uncertainty and supply constraints earn a mid-high score of 6.

evidence_list.snippet: As the duration and ongoing economic impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic remain uncertain, current and future budget priorities and funding levels for Government, Healthcare and Education customers may be adversely affected.

components.reason: Direct link to COVID-19’s uncertain duration and impacts.
Targets specific customer segments (Government, Healthcare, Education).
Highlights possible funding/budget reductions affecting sales.

evidence_list.reasoning_summary: Segment-specific budget risk tied to pandemic uncertainty justifies a 6.
